input: Those missing details remain unresolved even though current metabolic instability and persistent blood pressure are explicitly documented by the treating clinicians.
The patient describes nausea and fluctuating blur, and the planned work assessment has been interrupted for clinical care.
The driver cannot provide a reliable account of the latest diabetes medication change or a complete glucose log, and the visual symptoms have not received an independent specialist assessment.
The patient has confirmed type 2 diabetes and is acutely unwell at the current assessment.

The treating physician's signed note explicitly documents metabolically unstable diabetes after reviewing current observations and laboratory results; this is a documented clinical assessment rather than a diagnosis inferred by the nurse from thirst alone.
Clinical assessment suggests possible hearing impairment after the driver repeatedly missed spoken instructions, and audiometry has not been performed.
He can follow conversation better when facing the speaker, but neither an unaided better-ear threshold nor an aided standard is documented.
His employer's earlier form marked hearing satisfactory without describing a test; that form does not supply the missing audiometric measurements.
